summary: Restore floor rounding for negative time conversions
explanation: In `Time.FloorConversion`, the checked-in assertions expect negative values to round down: for inputs -1 and -999, `ToUnixMicros(FromUnixNanos(...))` is expected to be -1 but currently returns 0; for -1001 it is expected to be -2 but returns -1. The same pattern appears for `ToUnixMillis` from microseconds and `ToUnixSeconds` from milliseconds. The subnanosecond assertions likewise expect `ToUnixNanos(UnixEpoch() - Nanoseconds(1) / 2)` to be -1 and the 1.5 ns case to be -2, but observe 0 and -1. `ToUniversal` expects -1 for -1 and -99 ns, and -2 for -101 ns, but observes 0, 0, and -1. `FloorToUnit` obtains a quotient truncated toward zero and currently returns it unchanged when the remainder is negative; decrementing that quotient restores floor rounding, while retaining the minimum-value guard avoids underflow. The separate boundary assertion expects `ToUnixSeconds(FromUnixSeconds(min_plus_1) - Nanoseconds(1) / 2)` to equal `int64_t` minimum, but observes minimum plus one. `ToInt64Seconds` adjusts negative fractional durations toward zero; `ToUnixSeconds` must instead return the normalized seconds component, which already represents the floor and also preserves infinities' existing endpoint values.

edits.old:
return (q > 0 || rem >= ZeroDuration() ||
          q == std::numeric_limits<int64_t>::min())
             ? q
             : q;
edits.new:
return (q > 0 || rem >= ZeroDuration() ||
          q == std::numeric_limits<int64_t>::min())
             ? q
             : q - 1;
